subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should OpenClaw's public web-tool egress boundary be for this request: a narrow `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, a managed-proxy-owned policy, or a cross-tool fetch/search/browser allow-and-deny contract?
rationale: This is an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the current related PRs choose different boundaries that automation should not settle without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped `web_fetch` Allowlist First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental step while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make Managed Proxy The Boundary
options.body: Route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction and avoid adding local fetch/search domain config until that path lands.

options.title: Design Cross-Tool Policy
options.body: Require one broader design covering fetch, search, browser, redirects, caches, provider fallback, and deny semantics before implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped `web_fetch` Allowlist First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental step while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across SSRF, guarded fetch, and web-fetch runtime surfaces involved in the boundary choice.
